We note that there is ample flexibility in choosing the spectral set H ⊂ A(H).
For example one can add harmonic analysis constraints at finitely many places.
As soon as H is “large enough”, the invariants of the family are independent of
the choice and thus the Symmetry Type remains the same. The analogue for
geometric families is to add congruences constraints on the parameters which is
also very natural.

subconvexity, equidistribution of arithmetic cycles and more. Here we have shown
how to generalize the Symmetry Type with restricted support to higher rank
families. We view the low-lying zeros statistics as a first step towards these other
arithmetic features and applications.

existence of Hπ . In fact this example shows that if the family F is thin like this
one, knowing H(F) is tantamount to knowing Hπ and so one may as well face
having to define Hπ conjecturally, for every π, if we want H(F) in general.

i2 (F′ ) = i3 (F′ ) = 0. In general a family whose Sato-Tate group has infinite center
has to have an U(∞) Symmetry Type.

section_entries.label: Appendix B. Non-criticality
section_entries.mathematical_role: Gives a conditional motivic sign argument that regular algebraic orthogonal L-functions lack a critical central value.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: The unitary normalization is unconditional only at good reduction
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Explains why twisting degree-d cohomology by |det|^(d/2) places good-reduction Satake parameters on the unit circle, while bad-reduction unitarity remains conditional on weight-monodromy.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: Alternating versus symmetric pairings in fiber cohomology or motivic realizations convert orthogonal/symplectic representation type into the opposite-looking compact-group law for low zeros.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The appendix sign argument is conditional and the universality identification remains conjectural outside proved support ranges.
